glosses: to remelt (to melt down and remake; to make something again after melting it)
to melt down (to turn into a liquid one by one or completely)
to remelt, to melt again (to cause something to melt again)
to melt down (to gradually or completely lose one's original shape and structure due to high temperature)
to melt through (to go into or through something after melting)
to be remelted (to undergo melting again)

examples.text: Wieczorem, po siekierezadzie na zrębie i po siekierezadzie w szopie, gdzie porąbałem resztę kloców, stałem przy piecu w izdebce Babci Oleńki i przetapiałem na patelni smalec ten, co go wczoraj zakupiłem w sklepie.

glosses: To melt fully, especially metal or glass so that it can be remade into something else.

examples.text: The Great Exhibition of 1851 is also very much in King's Cross's DNA. The clock in its short, Italianate central tower came from the Exhibition and in its early years it struck the hours, but the bells were first silenced in the First World War and then melted down during the Second World War.

glosses: To lose structure by being heated to a molten state.
To have a breakdown; to collapse or fail utterly.
